title: Machine-Checked Sign-Vector Kernel and Exact-Rational Certificates for Flag Targets, Quasipolyhedral Non-Attainment, Frame Slices, and Acyclic Chamber DAGs
abstract: Brennan Dury (arXiv:2611.32976, November 24, 2026) constructed objective-driven acyclic digraphs on chambers of locally finite affine hyperplane arrangements: from each objective-bounded chamber c, a codimension-r flag at its optimal face F yields 2^r - 1 outgoing targets via a sign-flip rule, and both Euclidean and Frame strategies force escape to strictly higher optimal values in bounded steps. We deliver an explicitly scoped, zero-floating-point verification stack pairing two complementary layers. First, an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 kernel (HyperplaneTraversal.lean; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice; 5 zero-axiom, 1 [propext], 12 [propext, Quot.sound]) proves single-coordinate sign-closure poset axioms, combinatorial sign-flip counting/distinctness/containment identities, cleared integer/inductive laws of Section 2 Figure 2's quasipolyhedral non-attainment counterexample (l_n(x) = 2^{-(n+1)}(x-n-2)), and scalar algebraic projections of Lemma 4, Lemma 15, Lemma 17, Proposition 3 (lexLt3), and Theorem 3. Second, ARRANGEMENT-TRAVERSAL-CERT-1.0 performs full multi-dimensional exact-Q verification of codimension ranks, Figure 2 truncations, full-rank Frame slices, and strict-complementarity KKT chamber DAGs across 16 canonical certificates (0.110-1.003 ms)—including a fully specified 8-chamber 4-line central fan DAG (L=3)—while rejecting 66/66 live adversarial forgeries.
